delivery_not_guaranteed_note: Browser support, timing, and rate-limiting posture vary, so web push is described as optional and helpful rather than guaranteed receipt.
delivery_role_note: Browser-origin web push is an optional reminder and routing convenience that points people back to the current official voter-information page/help lane rather than acting as a standalone authority.

notification_classes.delivery_scope_note: Optional deadline reminder that always points back to the current official registration or vote-by-mail page.
notification_classes.superseding_posture: Time-sensitive reminders are grouped for replacement and always defer to the current landing page.

notification_classes.delivery_scope_note: Operational alert for closures or moved polling places that reopens at the current official locator/help route.
notification_classes.superseding_posture: Correction or all-clear notices explicitly supersede earlier disruption messages.

permission_boundary_note: Notification permission is treated as a browser/origin capability gate and does not by itself guarantee continuing subscription or delivery.
rate_limit_or_platform_variance_note: The office reviews browser/platform variance and current rate-limit posture before describing any class of push alert as reliable enough to mention publicly.
subscription_lifecycle_note: Subscriptions may expire, be revoked, or otherwise change outside the office’s control; users can still reach the current official answer/help lane without an active subscription.
superseding_withdrawal_note: Time-sensitive or corrected notifications are reviewed for replacement, expiration, or fail-open recovery so stale alerts do not quietly impersonate the current official rule.
unsubscribe_and_settings_note: Each reviewed subscription entrypoint keeps a clear stop-alerts or settings/help path.
web_push_surface_label: Example browser-origin web push posture for official voter information
